title: Config Morpher — tiered approval & staggered shadow-canary for Optimize recs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Optimize generates batching and KV-cache configuration suggestions that can materially reduce per-token cost but risk regressions in latency or quality. We need an orchestration that can: 1) validate suggestions against synthetic and sampled production traffic, 2) apply them in a staggered manner with shadow-canary testing, 3) escalate to human adjudication if safety thresholds are hit, and 4) enable deterministic rollback.

Goal: Build the 'Config Morpher' flow — a lightweight orchestrator that transforms Optimize suggestions into safe, staged changes with a formal approval escalation matrix. This ticket scopes the control plane component, operator UX hooks, and the canary/rollback playbook.

Success metrics (measurable):
- Net cost reduction attributable to auto-applied suggestions: +$Xk/month (baseline tracked in cost-dashboard link).
- False-positive rollback rate (auto-rollback without operator input) <= 3% in first 90 days.
- Mean time to human adjudication <= 20 minutes when manual approval required.
- No customer-facing error incidents caused by applied configs (0 incidents).

Design proposal (high level):
- Ingest: Optimize emits suggestion bundle (config delta + confidence score + payload signature). Config Morpher validates signature and matches policies.
- Two parallel validation paths: shadow-canary and synthetic regression tests. Shadow-canary routes 5% of live traffic to the suggestion variant in read-only mode (no external side-effects) and collects latency/throughput/quality signals. Synthetic regression runs deterministic prompt sets through the variant to detect hallucination/quality regressions.
- Tiered gating:
  * Tier 0 (auto-safe): low-risk changes (cache TTLs, non-critical batching params under preset thresholds) auto-enact after synthetic tests pass and cost benefit > threshold.
  * Tier 1 (operator-notify): medium-risk: requires automated canary and a 1-hour observation window before auto-enact; operator can veto during this window.
  * Tier 2 (human-approval): high-risk: changes affecting model routing, quantization profile, or cache eviction policies require explicit two-person approval.
- Approval matrix: A configurable adjudication matrix defined per-customer and per-project with escalation rules (e.g., if primary approver unavailable after 30 minutes, escalate to Secondary on-call).
- Transitions and rollback: If any monitored metric crosses pre-set breach thresholds during canary, the system: immediately halts promotion, marks suggestion as failed, auto-rolls back the variant traffic routing, and creates a P0 review ticket with relevant telemetry and diffs.
- Operator UX: Console widget with timeline, diff viewer, traffic split controls, and one-click emergency rollback. Audit log entry written for every step (who approved, snapshot of configs).

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for policy matcher and signature verification.
- Integration test using a local runtime fork that can spawn paired endpoints (control + variant) and replay recorded traces.
- Staging shadow-canary against synthetic replay of production traces with injected faults.
- Pilot: roll to 2 internal teams with non-critical workloads for 30 days.

Rollout steps:
1) Feature flag behind Optimize.autopilot.experimental.
2) Dry-run mode (no actual config apply) for 2 weeks with dashboard and alerts.
3) Internal pilot with operator review gating.
4) Gradual expand to external customers with opt-in.

Rollback playbook (operator-facing):
- Auto-rollback: triggered when safety thresholds breached (latency p95 increase > 20% OR error rate > 1% absolute OR quality regression delta > configured tolerance). System reverses traffic routing and posts a P0 with stack traces and link to interactive dash.
- Manual rollback: operator can trigger immediate revert via Console rollback button; system records snapshot and re-applies last-known-good config.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Shadow-canary traffic percentage trade-off: 5% balances signal vs impact, but customers with low traffic may need synthetic-heavy validation instead.
- Tier definitions & per-customer overrides: implement policy as data to allow fast change without code deploy.
- Cost of running parallel variant (extra GPU spend) vs value of reduced regressions. Consider a budget cap per suggestion evaluation.

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- PM: Jordan Lee (owner of Optimize roadmap)
- Design: Mei Chen (Console flows)
- SRE: Carlos Rivera (observability & rollback infra)
- Security: Priya Rao (audit & KMS handling)

Acceptance criteria:
- Config Morpher validates and simulates 100% of Optimize suggestions in dry-run mode and surfaces clear diffs in Console.
- Shadow-canary harness can run with traffic splits configurable to 0.1% increments and emits telemetry to optimize-canary-dash.
- Approval flow implements a configurable adjudication matrix and logs all approvals to audit-logs (immutable).
- Auto-rollback triggers for defined thresholds and performs a deterministic revert within 30s of detection in staging.

Links and artifacts:
- Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPT/Config+Morpher+Spec
- Quick prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/8412
- Canary dashboard (staging): https://dashboards.redwood.com/d/optimize-canary/staging
- Cost impact baseline: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-cost-baseline

Next steps (this ticket):
- Spike (2 days) to implement a lightweight shadow-canary harness and metric collectors.
- Prototype approval UI mockups with Design (1 week).
- Security review kickoff to validate audit logging and signature handling (ASAP).
